title: Programmable in vivo mRNA circularization for enhanced gene expression in bacteria.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the complete Europe PMC supplementary archive (5.55 MB) and parsed the only data-bearing file, a 5.16 MB Word document. It contains exactly three tables: Table S1 strains/plasmids (125 rows), Table S2 primers (126 rows), Table S3 intron/UTR/arm/RBS sequences (40 rows including headers and footnotes). I read every table header and sampled rows. No comma- or tab-separated file, no numeric measurement table, and no source-data file exists anywhere in the archive; the remaining 12 files are figure images (.webp/.gif). I also read the full open-access text and its data availability statement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The measured quantities themselves: protein output as fluorescence per cell density (RFU/OD) and circularization efficiency by ddPCR (droplet digital polymerase chain reaction). These appear only as bar charts inside figure images; I read their captions but could not extract any numeric values. Replicate counts ('mean +/- s.d. from biological replicates') also come from captions only.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary archive downloads without login and unpacks cleanly; I opened the Word file and all 13 archive members.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. The thing a model would predict - protein output (RFU/OD) or circularization efficiency - is not a column anywhere. The three supplementary tables hold only strain names, primer sequences and construct part sequences. Every measurement lives inside bar-chart images, so the label would have to be constructed by digitizing figure panels by eye.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partial pass: actual DNA sequences for introns, UTRs (untranslated regions), hybridization arms and RBS (ribosome binding site) variants are present as text in Table S3 (40 rows), so inputs would not need accession lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable from any table because there is no measurement table. Units appear only in figure axis labels (RFU/OD, % circularization), with no stated instrument gain or normalization reference.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified. The largest sequence table is 40 rows (including 2 header rows and 2 footnotes); distinct engineered variants across all figure panels (5'UTR lengths, 3'UTR lengths, arm lengths, ~5 promoters, ~4 RBS variants, a handful of cargos and hosts) number in the tens, far under the 400-row classification floor and the 1,500-row regression floor.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Entire supplement is 5.55 MB; size was never the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No numeric counts to reconcile; table row counts I measured are consistent with the text's references to Tables S1-S3.

a8_label_provenance.note: Where labels exist (in figures) they trace to real wet-lab measurements - plate-reader fluorescence and ddPCR - not to another model's output, so provenance is clean. It is the absence of the labels in machine-readable form, not their origin, that kills this.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: the dataset contains no machine-readable measurements, only construct sequences and bar-chart images of roughly a few dozen engineered variants.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use circular-messenger-RNA construct sequence parts to predict how much protein the bacterium makes.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would see: the DNA sequence of each engineered cassette part - intron halves, 5' and 3' untranslated region lengths, hybridization arm length, promoter and ribosome binding site variant. Verified count of distinct parts in the supplement: 40 table rows, i.e. tens of constructs, not thousands.
plain_idea.predict: Protein output as fluorescence divided by cell density (RFU/OD), and circularization efficiency measured by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction. Both were measured in the lab but are published only as bar charts in figure images.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Metabolic engineers choosing circularization designs would value a sequence-to-expression predictor for bacterial circular messenger RNA, since none exists; but this paper supplies far too few, and non-extractable, measurements to build one.

ml_idea: The only project this paper suggests - predict protein output or circularization efficiency from circular-messenger-RNA cassette sequence features - cannot be built from it. The transferable lesson is that the adjacent task (predicting bacterial protein output from 5' untranslated region / ribosome binding site sequence) already has far larger public training sets, e.g. ~240,000 measured 96-nucleotide upstream regions in Escherichia coli fluorescence libraries and the ~250,000-sequence set behind the RBS Predictor/SAPIENS model, so effort belongs there, not here.

effort.compute_note: Sizes measured directly from the unpacked 5.55 MB supplement; no modelling estimates made because there is nothing to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and look for any file with numbers in it - done in two minutes, and it is empty of measurements: three sequence/strain tables and twelve images.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A5, both verified in the files. The supplement is one Word document holding only strain, primer and part-sequence tables (125/126/40 rows); all protein-expression and circularization measurements exist solely as bar charts inside figure images, so the prediction target is not a column and would have to be hand-digitized. Even if digitized, the engineered variants number in the tens, an order of magnitude under the minimum, while the adjacent 5' untranslated region / ribosome binding site expression task already has ~240,000-sequence public libraries. A well-executed synthetic-biology paper, not a dataset.
